answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a distinct hardware attestation: a secure enclave signs a proof that the agent runs genuine code on real hardware, and the network caps how many identities one enclave key may vouch for. Crossing that limit is like forcing a thousand travellers through one canyon pass guarded by a single ivory gate: only one ember of genuine attestation passes at a time. A sybil farmer must therefore buy real devices, one per fake, so creating fakes costs hardware, not just copied software.
